publisher: New York State Department of State, Division of Corporations
ownership: Official public active-corporation and other business-entity records published through OPEN-NY
catalog_license: No dataset-specific license; governed by OPEN-NY Terms of Use, which grant a non-exclusive revocable license and permit lawful reuse without attribution, share-alike, preapproval, or technical restrictions.
source_access: Public anonymous read-only HTTPS metadata and SODA API endpoints documented by OPEN-NY.
allowed_use: official HTTPS metadata and selected-field SODA API queries
lawful redistribution of approved normalized fields under the OPEN-NY Terms of Use with source and semantic limitations retained
prohibited_use: using the data as legal documentation for bank loans, court cases, incorporation, or another legal purpose
representing extract membership as proof of current legal status, current operations, legality, solvency, public access, licensure, or an open storefront
representing a location address as a verified current physical operating site
representing this dataset as inactive or temporarily suspended entities, assumed names, every business operating in New York, or every U.S. business
exporting DOS process/service-of-process names or addresses, CEO names or addresses, registered-agent names or addresses, or the location-name line
merging organizations across sources without versioned evidence
attribution: Source: New York State Department of State, Division of Corporations, Active Corporations: Beginning 1800, via OPEN-NY.
retention: Indefinite for immutable selected-field source and approved normalized records unless an approved retention rule or OPEN-NY notice requires another treatment.
redistribution: Approved normalized fields may be redistributed under the OPEN-NY Terms of Use with source refresh timestamp, source checksum, provenance, field exclusions, and legal-status/address limitations retained; state marks, logos, and other protected presentation assets are not included.
personal_data_handling: The connector never acquires or publishes service-of-process, CEO/chairman, registered-agent, or location-name fields. Entity names and reported location street addresses can incidentally identify an individual or residence, so they retain purpose and non-site limitations.
